headline: HSC pass rate drops to 52.12% this year, down from 58.83% in previous year
summary: The results for the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations were announced today, revealing a significant decrease in the overall pass rate compared to last year.
details: The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations is 52.12 percent. This marks a decrease from last year's pass rate of 58.83 percent, according to sources from the education ministry.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon officially announced the results today after 11:00 AM at the Secretariat. Students can now check their results online and via SMS.
A total of 12,70,583 candidates were registered to take the examinations across 11 education boards this year. The written tests commenced on July 2 and concluded on August 8 for most boards.
However, some examinations under the Chattogram board were delayed due to severe flooding in the region. These postponed tests were subsequently held and continued until September 9.
caption:
This year's HSC and equivalent exams saw a pass rate of 52.12%, a noticeable drop from last year's 58.83%.

headline_marked: Father of former Air Force officer [[files murder case]] after son's body found
headline: Father of former Air Force officer files murder case after son's body found
summary: Tahsif Sawri's body was recovered from the Turag River; a younger acquaintance is now in custody as police investigate the circumstances of his death.
details: The father of former Air Force officer Tahsif Sawri has filed a murder case with Uttarkhan police against unidentified persons, three days after his son's body was found floating in the Turag River.

Tahsif's body was recovered from the Rajabari Ghat area on Wednesday. He had disappeared on Tuesday evening after leaving his house on a motorcycle to meet an acquaintance named Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip.
Dwip, who was the last person known to be with Tahsif, was detained by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) and later transferred to River Police custody.
According to PBI officials, Dwip confessed that while they were in a drug hotspot area in Tongi late Tuesday night, a police team chased them, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dwip fled.
Tahsif's motorcycle was recovered from the Mazar slum area of Tongi on Friday morning based on information provided by Dwip.

The River Police are now leading the probe into the death of the former officer, who had previously gained attention for allegedly sharing a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's departure from Bangladesh.
caption:
A former Air Force officer's body was found floating in the Turag River. Now, his father has filed a murder case.

The father of former Air Force officer Tahsif Sawri has filed a murder case with Uttarkhan police against unidentified persons, three days after his son's body was found floating in the Turag River.

Tahsif's body was recovered from the Rajabari Ghat area on Wednesday. He had disappeared on Tuesday evening after leaving his house on a motorcycle to meet an acquaintance named Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip.

Dwip, who was the last person known to be with Tahsif, was detained by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) and later transferred to River Police custody.

According to PBI officials, Dwip confessed that while they were in a drug hotspot area in Tongi late Tuesday night, a police team chased them, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dwip fled.

Tahsif's motorcycle was recovered from the Mazar slum area of Tongi on Friday morning based on information provided by Dwip.

The River Police are now leading the probe into the death of the former officer, who had previously gained attention for allegedly sharing a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's departure from Bangladesh.
